paragraphs.text: Spermatogenic failure-105 (SPGF105) is a form of male infertility characterized by asthenozoospermia, with reduced sperm motility. Affected men have shown asthenoteratozoospermia or oligoasthenoteratozoospermia, with sperm showing acrosome and flagellum malformations. Fertilization has been achieved by intracytoplasmic sperm injection (ICSI) (Qu et al., 2023; Gao et al., 2025; Wang et al., 2026).

paragraphs.text: Wang et al. (2026) reported a Chinese man with primary infertility and severe idiopathic oligoasthenoteratozoospermia. Semen analysis showed a volume of 4.3 mL, sperm concentration of 2.0 x 10(6)/mL, vitality of 16%, progressive motility of less than 1%, and 0% normal morphology. Abnormal heads were seen in 76.5% of sperm, abnormal neck and midpiece in 14%, and abnormal flagella in 62.5%. Reproductive hormones were normal, the karyotype was 46,XY, and there was no Y-chromosome microdeletion. Head abnormalities included microcephalic and conical heads, and tail defects included short tails, acutely angled curved tails, coiled tails, and tailless sperm. Transmission electron microscopy showed loss of the acrosome, a disorganized helical structure of the mitochondrial sheath, and disrupted or partly absent '9 + 2' microtubule structures in the axoneme.

paragraphs.text: Gao et al. (2025) performed whole-exome sequencing in a cohort of 105 Han Chinese men with idiopathic asthenoteratozoospermia and identified biallelic ADGB mutations in 3 infertile men from unrelated families. Sanger sequencing was also performed. One man was homozygous for a frameshift mutation (c.2801_2802del, K934Rfs*33), another was homozygous for a thr1056-to-ile (T1056I) missense mutation (c.3167C-T), and the third was compound heterozygous for T1056I and an ala1066-to-val (A1066V) missense mutation (c.3197C-T). The variants were rare in the general population and multiple bioinformatics tools predicted them to be damaging. In functional assays, the structural defects were associated with dysregulation of ADGB and of multiple spermatogenesis proteins.

paragraphs.text: Wang et al. (2026) performed whole-exome sequencing in 781 Chinese men with primary infertility and identified 148 ADGB variants. Using ACMG criteria, 6 of these were classified as likely pathogenic. Two of the likely pathogenic missense mutations were found in compound heterozygous state, confirmed by Sanger sequencing, in a man with oligoasthenoteratozoospermia: c.4859G-A, resulting in an arg1620-to-gln (R1620Q) substitution, and c.4981A-G, resulting in a lys1661-to-glu (K1661E) substitution. Arg1620 was conserved across vertebrates. Lys1661 was conserved in mammals but was replaced by glutamine, serine, and glycine in birds, amphibians, and fish, respectively. Western blot analysis showed no ADGB protein in the patient's sperm, and immunofluorescence showed reduced ADGB and PNA staining.

paragraphs.text: In a Chinese man with oligoasthenoteratozoospermia (SPGF105), Wang et al. (2026) identified compound heterozygous missense mutations in the ADGB gene: a c.4859G-A transition, resulting in an arg1620-to-gln (R1620Q) substitution, and K1661E. The mutations were found by whole-exome sequencing and confirmed by Sanger sequencing. The c.4859G-A variant had an allele frequency of 0.00285 in East Asians in gnomAD v4. It was predicted to be deleterious (CADD score 28.2), and arg1620 was conserved across vertebrates. ADGB protein was absent from the patient's sperm.

agent.process_note: I read all 3 papers in full. Qu et al. (2023) and Gao et al. (2025) are available only as abstracts. Wang et al. (2026) is a full text in Chinese with an English abstract. Qu et al. (2023) does not give the zygosity or the specific changes of the patient's variants, so no allelic variant is entered from that paper. No HGNC reference data were supplied, so the MIM number and chromosomal location of ADGB are omitted. None of the papers described parental segregation testing for the compound heterozygous cases. Autosomal recessive inheritance is inferred from the biallelic genotypes, not from a stated pedigree analysis.
